newsitem.title: DUBAI: United States and UAE launch wargames in the Gulf.
newsitem.headline: United States and UAE launch wargames in the Gulf.

text.p: The United States and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) have launched two weeks of naval exercises in the Gulf, a U.S. Navy spokesman said on Thursday.
"There are about 1,500 people from the U.S. Navy participating in the training," the spokesman told Reuters.
He would not say how many UAE forces were involved in the wargames, codenamed "Iron Magic '97". UAE officials were not immediately available for comment.

The navy spokesman said the exercises, which include three U.S. amphibious vessels, began on July 22 and would continue until August 4. He said the wargames did not include any other sections of the U.S. military.
The three ships -- assault ship Boxer, transport dock Ogden and landing craft Fort Fisher -- had been in the Gulf since May 20 and would remain for an unspecified period, he said.
"The ships are on a routine deployment to the Arabian Gulf," the spokesman said.

The UAE and the United States concluded a military pact in 1994, but full implementation has been hindered by obstacles including issues such as which country's laws would apply if U.S. military staff committed an offence in the UAE.
U.S. naval forces patrolling the Gulf often come to the UAE and defence sources say as many as 40,000 U.S. servicemen visit the UAE every year.
